first_meet: Vanakkam! You must be the grandchild from the old farm. I'm Kavitha — I run the store.
default: Fresh seeds for the season, just in. Take a look at what's growing well right now.
If it's in season, I stock it. If it's not, even I can't make it grow!
My cousin in the city buys whatever you ship. He says the valley's produce is the best he's tasted.
ugadi: Ugadi means new beginnings. A good time to plant something you've never grown before.
kharif: The monsoon keeps everyone busy. Paddy seed has been flying off my shelves!
rabi: Rabi is my favourite — cool mornings, mustard in bloom, and everyone is in a good mood.
winter: Winter greens sell quickly. Methi and radish grow fast in this cold.
rain: Rain again! Good for your fields, bad for my footfall.
hearts_4: You know, I've started setting aside the best seeds for you before the others get here.
hearts_8: Some days I think this valley only woke up again because you came back. Don't tell Murugan I said that.
birthday: You remembered my birthday? Nobody remembers the shopkeeper's birthday!
festival: Isn't the square beautiful today? I closed the store early — even I need a festival.
gift_loved: {item}! Oh, you shouldn't have — this is exactly what I love.
gift_disliked: Ah... {item}. I'll, er, find a place for it on a back shelf.

first_meet: Ah, the young one from the old farm! Your grandparents grew the sweetest watermelon in the valley.
default: Water your crops every day, or they'll just sit there sulking.
Ship what you grow in the chest by the plot — it sells overnight.
When the season turns, anything that can't take the new weather withers. Plan your planting!
ugadi: Okra and amaranth are forgiving. Start small, learn the soil.
kharif: Monsoon! Rain waters the fields for you — the best time of the year for paddy.
rabi: Toor dal and chickpea love the Rabi sun. My father grew nothing else.
winter: Winter is for greens, garlic and rest. Even the soil needs a nap.
rain: Hear that? That's the sound of free watering. Go fishing, the fields are taken care of.
hearts_4: You've got good hands. Your grandfather would be proud of that plot.
hearts_8: I've been farming here fifty years. I never thought I'd see someone make the old farm sing again.
birthday: For me? On my birthday? Aiyo, you'll make an old man cry.
festival: A festival day! No farming today — well, maybe a little watering.
gift_loved: {item}! Now that's a proper farmer's gift. Thank you!
gift_disliked: {item}? Hmph. I suppose it's the thought that counts.

first_meet: Oh, hello. I'm Devi. I make remedies from what the Ghats give us — if you find anything interesting on the trail, show me.
default: Turmeric, neem, amla... the forest is a pharmacy, if you know where to look.
The Ghats Trail is west of your farm. Different plants appear each season.
Paati says the Vanam Thay left when we stopped caring for the Panchayat Hall. I think she may be right.
ugadi: Neem flowers bloom around Ugadi. Bitter and sweet — just like the new year.
kharif: Mushrooms pop up after the rain. Only pick the ones on the trail, not the ones by the tank.
rabi: Amla season! One a day and you'll never need my remedies.
winter: Wild honey is at its best now. The bees on the cliffs are generous in the cold.
rain: The forest smells alive in the rain. Everything grows twice as fast out there.
hearts_4: I've been saving my grandmother's notes on the valley's herbs. Maybe I'll show you someday.
hearts_8: You listen to the valley, like I do. It's rare. I'm glad you're here.
birthday: You found out my birthday? That's... very sweet of you.
festival: Festivals remind me why the valley matters. Everyone together, just for a day.
gift_loved: {item}... this is perfect. I can make so much with it. Thank you.
gift_disliked: {item}. Hmm. I don't think I have a use for this.

first_meet_gift.line: Here — take my old rod. Face the pond on your farm or the Ghats river and cast with it.

first_meet: Hey! New face! I'm Ravi. I spend more time on the water than on land.
default: Hold the rod steady, and when the marker swings into the green, reel in!
The pond on your farm has tilapia and rohu. The Ghats river holds the rarer ones.
Some fish only bite when it rains. The best fishermen love bad weather.
ugadi: They say a Golden Mahseer still swims in the Ghats river. I've never caught one.
kharif: Monsoon means prawns in the river and magur in the ponds. Get out there!
rabi: Karimeen are back in the river. Pearl spot fry — nothing better.
winter: Cold water, slow fish. But the Golden Mahseer... winter is its season.
rain: Perfect fishing weather! What are you doing talking to me?
hearts_4: You're turning into a real angler. Next time, let's fish the river together.
hearts_8: You're the only one in the valley who gets why I love the water. Thanks for that.
birthday: My birthday! You're the best. Seriously.
festival: Food, music, and nobody asking me to fix their nets. Festivals are great.
gift_disliked: {item}? Uh... thanks, I guess? The fish might like it.

first_meet: Hello! I'm Anjali, I teach at the little school by the tank. The children are already talking about you.
default: The children want to know what you're growing. I told them to come see for themselves.
I've been teaching the history of the valley — the tank was built by a king nobody remembers.
If you look at the calendar in your journal (J), you'll never miss a birthday or festival.
ugadi: Happy new year! The school always opens again after Ugadi.
kharif: Monsoon holidays! Well, for the children. I still have papers to mark.
rabi: Deepavali is coming — the children are making paper lanterns for the square.
winter: Pongal is the best lesson in gratitude I know. Thank the sun, the rain, the cattle.
rain: The school roof leaks when it rains. One day we'll fix that too.
hearts_4: The children drew a picture of your farm. You're in it, with a very large watering can.
hearts_8: I used to think I'd leave the valley one day. Lately, I don't think about that at all.
birthday: A birthday present! You're so thoughtful. The children will be jealous.
festival: Look at the kolam the children drew! Aren't they wonderful?
gift_loved: {item}! How did you know? I love it!
gift_disliked: {item}... that's very kind, but it's not really for me.

first_meet: So you're the one who came back. I knew your grandmother, child. Come — see what's become of our Panchayat Hall.
default: The Panchayat Hall was the heart of Viralpadi. Now look at it — cracked walls and empty shelves.
Fill the Hall's offering baskets with what the valley gives, and the Vanam Thay may return.
Each season brings different gifts. The baskets ask for a little of everything.
ugadi: Eat your bevu-bella, child. Bitter and sweet together — that's what a year is.
kharif: The monsoon fills the old tank. The king who built it knew what he was doing.
rabi: When I was a girl, the whole valley lit lamps for Deepavali. We will again.
winter: Pongal is when we thank the land. Come to the square — bring something you grew.
rain: Rain on the roof. My knees knew it was coming before the clouds did.
hearts_4: You remind me of your grandmother. Stubborn, kind, always muddy.
hearts_8: When the Hall is whole again, I want you standing beside me. You've earned it.
birthday: At my age, every birthday is a gift. But this is a nice one too.
festival: This is how Viralpadi should always feel. Everyone together.
gift_loved: {item}! You spoil an old woman. Bless you, child.
gift_disliked: {item}? At my age? My stomach would never forgive me.
